title: Flight to Safety Begins, Private Credit Cracks & the Software Bloodbath Continues | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman sees defensive rotation beneath a flat index and expects private-credit liquidity restrictions to spread. He favors payment networks, Moody's proprietary franchises, Quanta infrastructure and Meritage value, while preferring Netflix without Warner Bros. His Nvidia operating outlook was supported. Conditional recession positioning is selective because AI-sensitive utilities and troubled health insurers may not behave defensively. He uses charts as a trigger to revisit fundamentals, while explicitly declining to forecast an imminent recession.
assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman is the sole substantive speaker; viewer questions are distinguished from his responses.
framework_points: Separate index performance from sector rotation.
Analyze redemption rights against asset liquidity.
Favor proprietary databases, duopolies and physical infrastructure.
Choose defensive businesses at the subsector level rather than rely on labels.
Use charts to revisit fundamentals and avoid newly collapsing stocks.
tools_and_charts: Carvana short interest and days to cover
transcript_cautions: Caption says Edison International/EIX then ConEd later; preserve the two named examples rather than silently treating them as the same utility.
The statement that no recession occurred since the GFC does not explicitly exclude the pandemic.
